name: Qurra ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Haywa'il al-Ma'afiri
nameAr: قُرّة بن عبد الرحمن بن حَيْوَئيل المَعافري المصري

laqab.en: Qurra is said to be a laqab, his given name being Yahya (Ibn Hibban, from Isma'il ibn Ayyash, through a weak chain; the Taqrib: «يقال اسمه يحيى»)

deathVariants.authority: Ibn Yunus: «يقال توفي سنة سبع وأربعين ومائة» (reported, not asserted); the Taqrib gives 147

verdicts.en: Weak in hadith. Elsewhere: lax in hearing and in hadith, but not a liar.
The reports he transmits are objectionable.

verdicts.ar: لم أر له حديثًا منكرًا جدًا، وأرجو أنه لا بأس به
verdicts.en: I have not seen a very objectionable report of his, and I hope there is no harm in him.

verdicts.ar: تفرد به قرة … وقرة ليس بقوي في الحديث … والمرسل هو الصواب
verdicts.en: Qurra alone transmits it, and Qurra is not strong in hadith; the mursal is the correct form.

flags.label: The disputed link
flags.detail: The whole argument over this hadith's connected chain is an argument about Qurra. Ibn Hajar's one-line summary, “truthful, but has objectionable reports”, is the balance of the verdicts above.

flags.label: Used by Muslim only paired
flags.detail: Muslim included him in one hadith only (Sahih Muslim 1591e), alongside Amr ibn al-Harith and others (maqrun), a sign that he was not relied on alone.

flags.label: Ibn Hajar on this report
flags.detail: “Qurra erred in it; the preserved version is Malik from al-Zuhri from Ali ibn al-Husayn, sent back without a Companion, as in the Muwatta.” (Ithaf al-Mahara 16/205)

bio: An Egyptian narrator who studied with al-Zuhri. Al-Awza'i is reported to have said no one knew al-Zuhri's hadith better; Ibn Hibban replied that everything he narrated from al-Zuhri does not amount to sixty hadith.
